title: Plant Intake, Quarantine and Source Verification

content.overview: Incoming clones, donor material and seeds can introduce identity errors or plant-health risk. Intake should preserve source and lot identity while unresolved biological risk remains physically or procedurally separated from established clean stock.

vocabulary.definition: Separation of incoming or suspect material until defined acceptance criteria are met.
A uniquely identified genetic or plant-material entry maintained with source and history.
Documented conditions that must be satisfied before material enters routine production.

sections.title: Identity begins at receipt
sections.body: Assign internal IDs and preserve supplier/source, claimed cultivar, generation or clone source, date and quantity instead of relying on tray labels alone.

sections.title: Clean-looking is not the same as verified clean
sections.body: Latent pathogens or pests may not be visible at intake. Inspection, appropriate testing strategy and observation period should match the risk of the material.

sections.title: Quarantine must be operationally separate
sections.body: A quarantine label alone does little if tools, runoff, people or plant contact freely connect incoming material with clean propagation.

workedExamples: A new clone line with no symptoms still receives its own accession ID and intake record before it is mixed with mother stock.
If quarantine plants share drainage and tools with production, the physical sign does not create meaningful isolation.
commonMistakes: Renaming incoming genetics before preserving source identity.
Releasing material based only on appearance.
Running quarantine and clean propagation with the same untracked tools.
content.practicalApplication: Create an intake checklist covering source, accession ID, lot, quantity, condition, inspection/testing plan, quarantine location, tool controls and release decision.
content.summary: Intake protects both genetics identity and crop health by combining traceability with real isolation and defined release criteria.
